packs.title: Desert, Design & Detail
packs.promise: Read granite, architecture, gardens and art across three separate outings.

q.s: Find three changing silhouettes without leaving the trail.
st: Start after the official trailhead opens. Read today’s notices and choose a turnaround time within 30 minutes.
On the open trail find three granite outlines: rounded, angular and one that changes as you move. Stop safely to look.
Return by the same trail. Sketch or describe the three shapes, naming the one that changed most.

q.s: Turn a brief browse into a tiny reading compass.
st: Enter during open hours and choose a public shelf that interests you.
Find three words on accessible book titles or in a book you may browse. Record the words privately and return books correctly.
Write a new two-sentence reading invitation using those words. Label it as your own invention, not a quotation.

q.s: Make a three-part sketch in Wright’s desert setting.
st: Check in for your booked Taliesin West tour; use only its admitted route and spaces.
During a permitted pause compare rough masonry, a roof line and natural light. Make a three-part sketch or written shape description.
Finish the tour at its own pace. Give your composition an original title and explain which part connects it most strongly to the desert.

packs.title: Old Town in Small Frames
packs.promise: Follow a canal, decode sculpture and turn Old Town details into small creations.

q.s: Turn still horse forms into a sequence.
st: Find the Bronze Horse Fountain without entering the street or basin.
Look at the five horse forms and choose three details suggesting movement: leg, neck, tail or angle.
Write a three-beat movement sequence using the details you see. Give it an original title.

q.t: A Rabbit With a New Angle
q.s: See a giant steel animal change with your viewpoint.
st: Locate One-Eyed Jack from the pavement.
From two safe positions find a feature that stays obvious and one that becomes harder to recognize as its angle changes.
Describe or sketch your two views. Add an original one-line caption about the most surprising angle.

q.s: Make a color score from art visible along the street.
st: Walk the public gallery sidewalks near Main Street and Marshall Way. Choose two windows with artwork visible outside.
Select three colors across the works and note the order your eye finds them. Do not copy an entire artwork.
Make an original three-color abstract sketch or a three-line color score. Keep entrances clear.
